answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a first-contact bridge rule: each epoch, an identity's reward unlocks only when a counterparty it has never transacted with before publicly endorses its work, like a reef that grows only where a new current reaches it. A whisper of self-praise inside a farm counts for nothing, because endorsements must come from outside the identity's prior graph. One honest agent needs a single genuine stranger; a farm with a thousand fakes must find a thousand new strangers every epoch, paying full outreach cost per fake.
